messages:
pagerduty-bot: HIGH: 5xx spike and TLS handshake failures detected for /v1/generate across multiple edge POPs. Threshold breached: 5xx rate > 8% for 5m. Potential external dependency (DNS/CDN) degradation. Paging ben (oncall).
ben (oncall): on it. looking at dashboards now. linking datadog panel: https://dd.example.com/dash/edge-errors
ben (oncall): logs show lots of TLS handshake timeouts and SNI-related resets. 10s+ TCP handshake times to some edge IPs.
frank (sre): confirming packet captures from our egress show RSTs to a subset of Cloudflare IPs and elevated RTOs. Could be routing flaps or an upstream CDN issue.
elena (product): do we have customer-impact numbers? which customers hit first?
nora (cs): two large customers reported 502s via support queue, they're in EU region. Escalating to CS leads.
ben (oncall): initial mitigation plan: 1) temporarily route EU traffic to alternate edge region via routing policy fallback; 2) increase origin keepalive TTL; 3) enable api-gateway fallback mode (serve cached responses for short TTLs). Starting step 1 now: 
ben (oncall): // command we ran: 
```
# adjust routing weight to fallback pool
curl -X POST https://internal-api/route/update -d '{"route":"/v1/*","primary":false,"fallback_pool":"eu-fallback"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```
opsbot: NOTE: routing update applied (request-id: r-13f4). Traffic shift started ~30s ago.
frank (sre): seeing drop in TLS errors on eu-fallback nodes, but overall egress to Cloudflare still intermittent. I'm running dig/nslookup tests.
frank (sre): `dig +short A api.redwood.example @1.1.1.1` returns different IPs with inconsistent TTLs, and some queries time out.
mike (platform): opening ticket with CDN/DNS provider; adding logs and pcap. Ticket: https://support.cloudflare.com/incident/INC-987654 (assigned). pinging their SRE.
elena (product): customer comms draft: "We're investigating a third-party CDN/DNS issue causing intermittent API errors for EU customers. We're actively routing traffic to fallback edges and will update in 30m." Want a short blameless note.
ben (oncall): status update to customers: emailed affected customers and posted temporary status page note.
nora (cs): two customers asked for ETA. No ETA yet — posted "under investigation".
frank (sre): also seeing increased error traces from our auth provider (Auth0) calls timing out when routed via the affected edges. Might be related to upstream peering affecting multiple vendors. Opening Auth0 support ticket as well.
ben (oncall): as mitigation, I'm enabling direct origin bypass for token validation calls so they go via an unaffected egress route: 
```
# disable proxy for auth calls
curl -X POST https://internal-api/config -d '{"auth_proxy":false}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```
opsbot: CONFIG CHANGE applied (auth_proxy=false). Note: this increases origin load.
frank (sre): Datadog metrics: 5xx steadily dropping from 9% -> 3% after fallback routing. Latency improved ~120ms median.
mike (platform): Cloud provider says they see packet loss in a handful of POPs and are routing their edge traffic away; ETA unknown. They're triaging with their peering partner.
elena (product): changing severity to SEV2 (wider customer impact but partial mitigation in place).
ben (oncall): preparing handoff — my shift ends in 40m. Need someone to own next steps: keep pressure on CDN vendor, validate TLS handshakes across regions, confirm no config regressions, and draft external status updates.
frank (sre): I'll take the handoff. I'll continue running capture jobs and coordinate with vendor SRE.
ben (oncall): handoff notes: routing fallback performed, auth proxy bypass enabled, origin keepalive increased, affected POPs: AMS, FRA, LHR, some US-EAST intermittent. Key dashboards: https://dd.example.com/dash/edge-errors, https://dd.example.com/dash/latency-by-pop.
mike (platform): adding troubleshooting artifacts to the ticket: pcap s3://redwood-incident/1875004321/edge-rst.pcap, dig logs, req traces.
frank (sre): next actions: 1) validate Cloudflare's mitigation timeline; 2) run synthetic checks from multiple vantage points (EU/US/APAC); 3) roll back auth_proxy bypass once stable; 4) prepare a post-incident timeline.
elena (product): customer impact assessment: ~6% of total requests in last 45m, concentrated EU customers and mobile clients on certain carrier ISPs. No data loss, transient errors only.
nora (cs): prepping customer messages for impacted accounts with instructions for retry/backoff.
ben (oncall): final pre-handoff note: keep escalation path open (Cloudflare INC-987654), if error rate >7% for next 15m, escalate to execs.
pagerduty-bot: REMINDER: on-call handoff scheduled at 1875007080.
frank (sre): acknowledged. I'll update the incident channel with status every 15m and close once metrics stable for 30m.
mike (platform): follow-up: we should consider adding multi-CDN routing to reduce blast radius; filing a post-incident action item.
elena (product): agreed, add to roadmap items for reliability work.
opsbot: INCIDENT UPDATE: 45m since alert. Current 5xx rate: 2.9%. TLS handshakes failing: 0.7%. Routing fallback holding. Cloud provider marks degraded but stabilizing.
frank (sre): closing note for now — keeping incident open; monitoring-only. Will publish postmortem draft tomorrow.
ben (oncall): thanks all — good handoff. :thumbsup:
